phases.acceptance: Pairing-token auth, loopback-only registration, path-traversal guard on captureId, body size cap. See plans/2026-09-08/03-extension-crawler.md security requirements.
phases.note: DONE 2026-09-08, direct execution. Routes live in apps/shell/lib/swimcloudCaptureRoutes.ts (server.ts registers them; the module exists so the five security guards are testable -- server.ts starts its server at import time and nothing in it can be exercised in isolation). isLoopbackHost moved verbatim to apps/shell/lib/loopbackHost.ts so the registration gate and the exposure warning share one implementation. /parse deliberately NOT built (no consumer until Phase 4). Two real ordering traps found and fixed, not invented for the test: (1) body-parser is a no-op once req.body is set, so a route-level express.json mounted below server.ts's app-wide 50mb one would have silently inherited 50mb -- the router is mounted BEFORE the global parser AND carries its own Content-Length guard, with a test that mounts it in the wrong order and asserts the 2mb cap still holds; (2) captureIdForSubject interpolates a team subject's `season` straight into a filename, and clipboardPayload.ts validates season only as `typeof === 'string'`, so a hostile season would have produced a traversing captureId the server derived itself -- the derived id is validated exactly like a path parameter, plus a SEASON_PATTERN charset guard. CORS decision: NO headers by default. 03-extension-crawler.md's 'Where the crawl loop actually runs' puts the localhost POST in the MV3 background service worker with host_permissions for http://127.0.0.1/*, which is not subject to page CORS -- an Access-Control-Allow-Origin there would be decoration on a security header. OMNI_SWIMCLOUD_EXTENSION_ORIGIN opts in to a narrowly-scoped origin if an extension build ever posts from a content script instead; no placeholder id is invented. phases.name: Friction fix: batch the chrome.downloads fallback, pre-flight pairing check
phases.acceptance: A real 234-page crawl against an unpaired extension no longer produces 234 chrome.downloads popups with zero warning; it blocks pre-flight with a clear choice, shows a live running count if the coach proceeds anyway, and combines every fallback page into one file at the end.
phases.note: User hand-tested a real crawl and reported '234 pop ups'. Root-caused from the real code, not guessed: (1) background.ts's relayPage treated a chrome.downloads fallback as an unqualified success identical to a real app save, so totalFailures never incremented and no warning ever fired; (2) formatResumeDegradationLine had a typed 'app-unreachable' case with no message, falling through to empty string. Fixed: a pre-flight gate reusing the crawl's existing first round trip (no new network cost), a live downloadsFallbackCount distinct from totalFailures, and background.ts accumulating fallback pages in chrome.storage.local (not memory, since an MV3 service worker can be killed between messages) keyed per-page with a small index, flushed into ONE combined download by finishCrawl on every one of the crawl's 6 exit paths, not just the happy one. manifest.json gained unlimitedStorage. Full writeup: plans/2026-09-09/WORKLOG-13-friction-fix-download-batching.md. Real Chrome+extension click-through remains unverified -- no headless-extension harness exists in this repo, stated honestly per every prior worklog's same boundary.

phases.name: Scoring-correctness fix: exclude ambiguous prelims/finals duplicates from SwimCloud meet import
phases.acceptance: A swimmer with more than one swim of the same labeled event on a swims-list page is never scored twice; every excluded swim is named in a new skip reason rather than dropped silently.
phases.note: User reported a real import as '188 warnings... not clean... does not identify prelims vs finals... make sure the point numbers are correct.' Full diagnosis and fix in plans/2026-09-10/01-SWIMCLOUD-SCORING-CORRECTNESS.md. Root cause confirmed against the real fixture, not guessed: the swims-list page has no round/session column, so a swimmer who swam both prelims and finals of one event gets two (sometimes three) undifferentiated rows -- 6 groups, 13 of 30 rows (43%) on the one archived page. swimCloudMeetImportBridge.ts never set roundSwam on these rows, so packages/core's classifyRoundTier saw tier 'UNK', which canScoreAthlete treats as fully scoring (correct default for the PDF pipeline, wrong here) -- every duplicate was being scored as an independent finish using SwimCloud's Place column, which is itself proven to be a per-round placement, not the event's true field place (Nojus Skirutis: a faster swim marked '2nd', a slower one marked '1st', on two different swim ids). Also found: SwimCloud's numeric event/{n} id does not identify a labeled event 1:1 (Oskar Cebula's '100 Y Breast' splits across event/26/ and event/100/), so any fix must group duplicates by event LABEL, not event id. Fix: swimCloudTeamMeetSwimsToSwimmerResults now groups by (athlete, team, event label) and excludes every swim in a group of more than one, reporting each via a new 'ambiguous-round-duplicate' skip reason with a detail field (time/place/swim id) -- no guess is made about which swim is prelims vs finals, per CLAUDE.md's provenance rules. Also audited (no code change needed): exhibition-swim handling is correctly isolated end to end (ncaaScoringRules.ts's Rule 7-10-1 removal; the Hy-Tek leading-X time-token marker kept distinct from the unrelated 'Extracted' X badge chip) but the Hy-Tek detector remains unverified against real SwimCloud markup -- no real exhibition swim has been captured yet. '188 warnings' itself is not a defect: confirmed to be a raw per-page-warning-line count aggregated across an entire multi-page capture, dominated by expected/benign codes like relay-legs-absent; flagged as a UI follow-up (breakdown by code/severity, surface skip reasons visibly), not fixed this pass. The real, non-interim fix -- parsing /results/{meetId}/event/{n}/, which SwimCloud does label Preliminaries/Finals -- is scoped in the plan doc's section 6 but not started; it needs fixture F9 captured first.

phases.acceptance: New parser for /results/{meetId}/event/{n}/ (F9 fixture) extracting round-labeled results (A/B/C Final, Preliminaries) and the real A/B-Final meet Score; meet-scoped parallel fetching of every unique event id a crawl encounters (once per meet, not once per team); swimCloudTeamMeetSwimsToSwimmerResults resolves roundSwam/meetScore from the event page instead of excluding the ambiguous-round-duplicate group, falling back to phase 10's exclusion only when the event page wasn't captured.
phases.note:
User pushed back directly on phase 10's 'we can't know which round this is' and captured the missing page themselves 2026-09-10 (fixture F9, see its entry above). CONFIRMED: one page per Finals-labeled event holds every round as separate blocks; caption text maps directly onto the existing classifyRoundTier vocabulary; A/B Final tables carry the real meet Score in a u-is-hidden (rendered-hidden, markup-present) column -- the first page type in this pipeline with genuine per-swim meet points; exhibition is marked by a X REPLACING the rank-cell ordinal, not the leading-X-on-time-token Hy-Tek guess parser.ts's readTime currently makes -- that guess needs correcting. Also confirmed: SwimCloud's numeric event id is a results-PAGE id, not a round id -- a swimmer's third team-swims-list row (Oskar Cebula, 100 Y Breast, event/100/) sits under a wholly separate, unlabeled event id this meet's own sidebar groups with other suffix-less high-numbered ids (100-939), matching packages/core/src/lib/utils.ts's already-documented post-meet-time-trial numbering finding (isOutsideScoredProgram/scoredEventNumberMax) -- treat it as a likely time trial, not a third real round, until that page is captured. User's explicit requirement: parallelized, fast per-event fetching that scales to a big meet without becoming slow -- reuse the existing bounded-concurrency pool (extensions/swimcloud-companion/src/boundedFetchPool.ts, 3 lanes/400ms stagger, wired for swimmer-times in Phase 5/WORKLOG-09) rather than inventing a second mechanism. Full scoped build plan in plans/2026-09-10/01-SWIMCLOUD-SCORING-CORRECTNESS.md section 6. DONE 2026-09-10, executor, across two sittings split by a session rate limit (the limit hit between the last route test being identified and being written; zero work was lost -- the resumed session found the parser, bridge and crawl wiring already on disk and compiling, and wrote only the one missing test). FIVE LAYERS BUILT, all against the real F9 capture and nothing else: (1) PARSER -- parseMeetEventResultsHtml in packages/swimcloud/src/parser.ts, confidence 'real-capture-verified', 40/40 rows and 0 warnings on the real page. Splits the page into its four
ROUND-labelled round tables in PRINTED (program) order, not chronological -- Preliminaries swam first and prints last, and nothing re-sorts it. Caption text is kept VERBATIM ('A Final' / 'Preliminaries') rather than mapped to a tier here, because packages/core's classifyRoundTier already owns that vocabulary and a second copy could only drift from the first. (2) THE POINTS DISTINCTION, which is the correctness core of this phase. A/B Final tables carry a 'Score' header (real meet points: 20/17/16/15/14/13/12/11 and 9/7/6/5/4/3/2 on the real page); C Final and Preliminaries carry 'Pts' (SwimCloud's 0-1000 power index, title='Swimcloud Points'). These are different quantities and the page prints both. Each round records which it had via SwimCloudEventRoundPointsColumn ('score' | 'pts' | 'none'), meetScore is populated ONLY from a 'score' column, and a non-scoring round's meetScore is ABSENT rather than zero. Storing a 709 power index as meet points would have multiplied a team score. (3) EXHIBITION, read from the rank cell as F9 showed, NOT from the leading-X-on-time-token Hy-Tek guess. The marker REPLACES the ordinal, so an exhibition row legitimately has no place at all -- absent, never 0, and never a parse failure. readTime's separate Hy-Tek guess was left alone rather than 'corrected' as the fixture note anticipated: it is a different page family's convention, no real SwimCloud page has yet been captured that exercises it, and changing it on this evidence would be a guess. All five C Final swimmers are exhibition on the real page and the same five reappear marked in Preliminaries, so SwimCloud tags a swimmer consistently across every round on one page. (4) THE JOIN. parseMeetEventResultsHtml builds the SAME '{meetId}:swim:{id}' swimKey shape parseTeamMeetSwimsHtml builds, deliberately, so the two page types join on SwimCloud's own swim id with no normalization. buildSwimCloudEventRoundIndex turns a capture's event parses into that lookup, and swimCloudTeamMeetSwimsToSwimmerResults consults it BEFORE the phase-10 duplicate test -- a resolved swim is no longer ambiguous, so it is scored with its real roundSwam instead of excluded. Name+team+time was explicitly NOT offered as a fallback join: a swimmer who goes the same time in prelims and finals is exactly the hardest case, and such a match would be broken by map iteration order -- a coin flip deciding whether a swim scores. A swim with no id on either side stays unresolved and keeps phase 10's visible exclusion. (5) CRAWL. planMeetEventResults is MEET-scoped, not team-scoped, and dedupes repeated event refs: one event page holds every team's swimmers, so a per-team plan on a 40-team/42-event meet would fetch 1,680 pages to learn what 42 pages say. It takes no gender parameter -- an /event/{n}/ page is already one gender's event, and the page's own gender toggle points at a DIFFERENT event id (100/400 here) rather than a ?gender= variant, so a gender parameter would be inventing one. The crawler collects refs from each parsed swims list (swims[].event.eventRef, the only place a swims row names its results page) and runs the resulting steps through the EXISTING boundedFetchPool at 3 lanes / 400ms stagger, per the user's speed requirement -- no second concurrency mechanism was invented. DEVIATIONS AND OPEN GAPS, stated plainly rather than papered over: - DIVING: no diving event has been captured. A diving page's 'Score' could plausibly be the judged score (a 300.15) rather than meet points, and storing that as meet points would silently multiply a team score. So a diving event's Score column is read, reported as the warning 'diving-score-column-unverified', and deliberately NOT stored in meetScore. Nothing about diving-row markup is invented. - SINGLE-ROUND TIMED FINALS: expected to print one table with NO round caption, but never captured. An absent caption raises 'missing-round-caption' and the round stays absent -- it is never renamed 'Finals' on a guess. That round then contributes nothing to the join index, so its swims keep phase 10's exclusion behavior. - DQ / SCRATCH: F9 contains NO DQ, NS or SCR row, so no assertion in this phase claims to cover one. Such a time cell goes through the same shared readTime path every other page uses; that path is not newly verified here. - RELAYS: F9 is an individual event. A relay event's per-event page is unseen. A title='Leadoff' badge is still read if one appears, rather than assumed absent. - PAGINATION: F9 carries no c-pagination widget -- all four rounds and 40 rows arrived on one page. Whether a very large event's page ever paginates is UNPROVEN, so planMeetEventResults plans no page range. - The OpsModule clipboard path passes NO eventResults (a single pasted swims page has no event pages with it), so it keeps phase 10's exclusion behavior unchanged. Only the capture-picker path resolves rounds. This is correct, not an oversight -- but it means a coach pasting one page still sees ambiguous-round-duplicate skips. - OQ-9 (the nested /event/{n}/{subIndex}/ URL shape) is still unmodelled and still not blocking: nothing in this crawl produces such a URL.
